Level 4 · Defend

Level 4: Agentic Security Operations Professional

Detect, investigate, contain and recover from incidents where the actor is an agent.

Open the live courseSee pathways

Three core lessons live; telemetry and simulation labs in design

Who it is for
SOC analysts, detection engineers, incident responders and cloud security engineers.
Before you start
Level 1 plus SOC or engineering experience, or Level 2.
Capstone evidence
A live incident simulation with injects, time-boxed decisions, evidence handling and a post-incident report.
How it is assessed
Observed simulation scored on containment quality, evidence handling and the written review.

Modules and evidence

Each module ends in an artefact that goes into your portfolio.

ModuleYou will be able toEvidence
Telemetry engineeringDefine privacy-conscious event schemas for runs, tool calls, identity, policy decisions, retrieval provenance, model versions and approvals.Event schema and sample trace
Detection engineeringDetect anomalous tool sequences, privilege escalation, unusual delegation, exfiltration, poisoning indicators and agent loops.Detection set mapped to MITRE ATLAS
Threat huntingCorrelate agent traces with identity, cloud, endpoint, network, application and data-access telemetry.Hunt report
ForensicsPreserve chain of custody; reconstruct sequences; separate model output from executed actions; find affected data and credentials.Forensic timeline
ContainmentRevoke tokens, disable tools, quarantine agents, isolate execution, freeze workflows and restore known-good state.Containment plan executed in a controlled environment
Recovery and learningValidate eradication, reissue credentials, restore memory safely, retest controls and update threat models.Post-incident review

Live lessons for this level

3 lessons in the live course are currently mapped to this level.

  • 15Monitoring, detection and digital forensics
  • 17Incident response, containment and recovery
  • 25Runtime Monitors and Honest Detection

The free lessons open without payment. Lesson order inside the course is by module, not by level.

Planned lessons

These lessons are specified but not yet published. They address gaps identified in the curriculum review.

  • P8Detection engineering with MITRE ATLAS Planned
    Turning agent traces into detections and response playbooks, including the MITRE OpenClaw case studies as worked examples.
  • P4Privacy, sensitive data and logging in agent systems Planned
    Prompt and log retention, leakage, minimisation, deletion, training reuse, residency and access control as data moves between tools, providers, logs and retrieval stores.
